This is a nonrandom independent re-review of **16 saved native-size PNGs**: 13 prior positives from sibling reviewers across seven families, two known failures and one unresolved case. Sources, original bytes, fresh observations and 15 ordinary v2 image-review receipts are retained here. The prior verdicts were visible for stratification; this is not a blinded accuracy estimate. The Wardley failure is a regression control previously reviewed by this author. Reviewer names in the old receipts are generic; their exact original file/line provenance is recorded in `sample.json`.

One prior positive was wrong: native requirement 352 renders vertically despite explicit `direction LR`. The pinned documentation defines LR as Left to Right. The shared source projection had made that request advisory. The narrow fix restores it, changes only that occurrence's expectation identity and invalidates both old admissions. Fresh direct reviews give Mermaid correct and native incorrect. The two original positive receipts remain untouched in `prior-352-reviews.jsonl`; immutable B0 is unchanged.

The other outcomes agree with the saved reviews: twelve correct, two existing failures, one unresolved per-edge interpolation case. Permitted differences include wrapping, dimensions, default skins and treemap opacity; no reference image supplies an expected answer. Full source facts and the actual PNGs were inspected, including owned labels, topology, marks, fields and quantities. The unknown keeps its interpolation obligation.

Run `bun test tests/png-independent-validation.test.ts tests/visual-expectation.test.ts tests/docs-source-review.test.ts`. The first test imports the new judgments and checks ordinary assessment; hashes/admission verify binding, **not meaning**. A separate executable image probe decodes the two actual requirement PNGs at 1:1 and measures all chromatic body components before applying direction. Human image review supplies caption-to-body ownership. The bounded two-body proof has equivalent translation/scale, wrong-axis/reflection and ambiguous-overlap controls; it makes no claim about arbitrary graph layouts. No project SVG, renderer call, OCR or reference agreement supplies the PNG judgment.

Images originate from Mermaid's MIT-licensed pinned syntax examples and the retained public outputs. The literal sources and source pin are in `sample.json`; the upstream license is retained at `corpus/docs-assets/MERMAID-LICENSE`. This small sample provides no correctness claim for unviewed outputs or a measured corpus error rate.
